articles.title: Maresca says he would describe Manchester City as ‘cheats’ if he was a United fan
articles.summary: Manager claims City fans suffering more than players. Captain Rúben Dias: ‘We’re calm. We trust the club’ Enzo Maresca has admitted he would describe Manchester City as “cheats” if he were a Manchester United or Arsenal fan.
body: Maresca guided City to an impressive 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday in their first game since the club ere found guilty of more than 100 charges related to breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules. He was asked whether the performance was down to the team being brought closer together by the guilty verdict.

“It probably has been more tough for our fans than for the players or for me as it’s more complicated,” he said, “because if I am an Arsenal fan or a United fan and you are a City fan, I can tell you: ‘Hey, my friend, you cheat’ – or this kind of thing. But we were happy at the end of the game and inside the changing room. We were very happy celebrating the three points because we know how difficult it is at Anfield.”

City, who have appealed against the independent commission’s ruling and continue to protest their innocence, have drawn criticism for the exuberant manner of Sunday’s celebration. Maresca defended the revelry but is conscious of the need to focus on Wednesday’s visit of Paris Saint-Germain in their second Champions League game of the season, following their 2-0 victory at Porto.

articles.title: F1 returns to Africa for first time since 1993 with 10-year Rwanda deal from ‘early 2030s’
articles.summary: African Grand Prix will take place at new track near Kigali. Stefano Domenicali: ‘Today is a landmark moment for F1’ Formula One has confirmed Rwanda will join the calendar, having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting to be hosted on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the…
body: The meeting, to be known as the African Grand Prix, will be held on a circuit in Bugesera, approximately 40km south of the capital, Kigali, and represents a successful conclusion to the sport’s long-held ambition to return to the African continent, which Lewis Hamilton has championed.

F1 last raced in Africa at Kyalami in South Africa in 1993 and the seven-time world champion Hamilton has been outspoken in his belief that F1 should return, working behind the scenes to facilitate it.

“For the past six or seven years I’ve been fighting in the background to get a grand prix, sitting with stakeholders and asking the question: ‘Why are we not in Africa? There’s one on every other continent, why not Africa?’” he said earlier this year.

The Rwanda track will be designed by WurzDesign, run by the former driver Alexander Wurz, but no specific date has been set for the first race, with F1 only stating the “early 2030s”. That timescale allows for it to be built and then homologated to full FIA Grade 1 status, with a rendition of the circuit indicating an intent for it flow across the natural contours of the landscape.

articles.title: Netflix secures 2030 World Cup TV rights in Spain
articles.summary: Netflix will broadcast World Cup games for the first time in 2030 as it secures the rights to show World Cup games in co-host Spain and Andorra.
body: Streaming platform Netflix has secured the rights to broadcast the 2030 World Cup in Spain and Andorra.
It is the first time the subscription-based platform will show the men's World Cup.
"We will offer all 104 matches of the world's biggest football competition live," Netflix said in a statement.
Reigning champions Spain will co-host the 2030 World Cup with Portugal and Morocco. Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay will also stage matches to celebrate the tournament's centenary.

articles.title: Manchester City v PSG is a reminder of the path not taken in sanctions battles
articles.summary: Gulf-owned clubs have faced Uefa scrutiny – their different approaches since have left one at the top table and one raging against the machine. Nasser al-Khelaifi was among those unhappy with the timing of the release of Manchester City’s guilty verdict by the Premier League a fortnight ago…
body: The two clubs are linked by more than their ownership by Gulf states, being among the first found to have broken Uefa’s financial fair play rules in 2014, and by a magnitude that would make subsequent offenders pale in comparison.

Uefa’s investigators found that between 2011 and 2013, when the maximum permitted loss for a club playing in European competitions was €45m (£38m), PSG’s deficit was €218m and City’s €188m, yet both clubs avoided charges by signing settlement agreements.

With hindsight the terms seem generous to say the least, with sanctions limited to a financial penalty of €20m each, plus more onerous restrictions on their spending in subsequent years. City and PSG were made liable to pay a further €40m if they broke the terms of their settlements.

articles.title: ‘It changed me a lot’: how Japan’s academy system supercharged women’s team
articles.summary: The Women’s Asian Cup winners continue to punch above their weight thanks to innovative youth development. Japan have constantly pushed the boundaries in women’s football, whether it be with regular success in Asia or their ability to beat the biggest nations in the world.
body: Nadeshiko won the Women’s World Cup in 2011 and reached another final in 2015, while more established countries fell by the wayside. Japan have not replicated that success but did win the Women’s Asian Cup this year under the guidance of Nils Nielsen, who has since been succeeded by Michihisa Kano, and most of the biggest stars play outside the country, with 24 contracted to Women’s Super League clubs alone.

Japan are discreet about the secrets behind their success, particularly the easy-on-the-eye style that has become a trademark of the men’s and women’s teams, but one of those secrets lies in the Japanese Football Association (JFA) creating the JFA Academy.

There are three that take girls across the country of 123 million people: Fukushima, Sakai and Imabari. A fourth, Kumamoto Uki, is a boys’ academy only. Fukushima was the first to open, in 2006, with Sakai following in 2012 and Imabari in 2015.

articles.title: Different ways to win - what Rugby League World Cup success looks like
articles.summary: Some teams have their eyes on a trophy - others are prioritising longer-term gains. BBC Sport assesses a Rugby League World Cup that comes at a pivotal time for the international game.
body: "Do I believe we can win? It's not a no. Anybody who says we can't win with a finality to it - that's not my belief."

England's new men's head coach Brian McDermott has sounded a note of hope going into the Rugby League World Cup. And he is not the only coach looking forward with optimism. For now at least, everybody harbours a dream.

Not everyone taking part in the men's, women's and wheelchair tournaments over the next month is expecting to come away with a winner's medal - but they all have a target for success. For some, it's a title. For others, it's showing progress, or creating a legacy.
The men's competition kicks off first, on Thursday (10:05 BST), with reigning champions Australia facing New Zealand in a Sydney blockbuster dubbed a potential dress rehearsal for the final.

articles.summary: Manager Enzo Maresca reacts to criticism of Manchester City's celebrations after their win at Liverpool by saying: "What do you want us to do?"
body: Sunday's match at Anfield was City's first game after an independent commission found the club guilty of charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.
After the 3-0 win, Erling Haaland looked close to tears in front of City's fans - which included his father Alf-Inge - while Maresca pumped his fists in jubilation.
"Criticised for what?" replied Maresca when asked for his response to City's celebrations being questioned by pundits and the media.
"We work every day to win games. It's the only thing that we can think about and be focused on.

articles.title: Jerry Jones defends man who called Dak Prescott ’embarassing’
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys lost 24-16 to a shorthanded Tampa Bay Buccaneers squad that was forced to start rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels on Thursday. After one of the biggest upsets of the year, a viral interaction between Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott and a fan who was working the game as a cart…
body: Although it hasn’t been confirmed, rumors hit social media that the employee in question was allegedly fired after the exchange, something Cowboys legend Michael Irvin addressed on First Take.
“I don’t like that he took that other guy’s job because he said it was embarrassing…It was embarrassing. So, don’t get mad at him,” Irvin asserted.

“Don’t fight him. Go back on that football field and fight those damn guys on that field, not that poor guy that just shared his thoughts. His thoughts were all of our thoughts, everybody in Cowboys Nation. That was embarrassing.”

Irvin isn’t alone in supporting the employee in question, either. Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones, who told reporters after the loss that the result was “extraordinarily disappointing,” has also come to the employee’s defense.

articles.title: Bethell returns as England call up youngsters Jack and Rew
articles.summary: Jacob Bethell will return for England's white-ball tour of Australia, while there are also first international call-ups for exciting prospects Thomas Rew and Eddie Jack.
body: Warwickshire's Bethell has not played since suffering a knee injury in July but is back as part of a near-full-strength squad for three one-day internationals.

England have made changes for the five T20s, resting players ahead of the Test tour of South Africa, meaning 18-year-old Somerset wicketkeeper-batter Rew and Hampshire's 21-year-old pace bowler Jack are included.
"Thomas Rew is an amazing young talent," national selector Marcus North told the Test Match Special podcast. "He has a great maturity around him for an 18-year-old.

"Eddie Jack is another great example of a system that has been supporting and developing our fast bowlers. This is an exciting time – it's always great when you get an opportunity to bring some players in."

articles.title: Josh Allen names who is the ‘greatest thrower’ of football in NFL history
articles.summary: As questions are being asked about Josh Allen’s throwing ability following Monday night’s game at SoFi Stadium, the Buffalo Bills’ quarterback has made it clear who the best thrower of all time is. Allen only attempted 19 throws during Monday Night Football and completed just 12 of those.
body: A return of 210 yards and one touchdown was subsidised by Allen’s rushing efforts but it was a masterclass on offence from Matthew Stafford for the Los Angeles Rams. The veteran quarterback threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns.
Having seen exactly how it is done by Stafford, Allen spoke after the game about what quarterback he feels is truly the best thrower of the ball.

Allen developed a reputation of having games in the past where he threw some questionable throws. Monday was one of those nights as he was labelled as throwing an ‘arm punt’ by Pat McAfee inside the first half.
It was apparent that Allen was left seriously impressed with what he watched from Stafford during the game, though.

articles.title: Report: Juventus already seeking a new centre-forward to support Kolo Muani
articles.summary: Reports from various outlets in Italy claim that Luciano Spalletti still wants Juventus to bring in another option at centre-forward as he seeks ways to help bring the best out of summer signing Randal Kolo Muani.
body: The centre-forward role has been a conundrum that has burdened Spalletti ever since he took over at Juventus just shy of one year ago.

The club were unable to prevent Dusan Vlahovic from walking away for free at the end of his contract, Jonathan David and Lois Openda were sent out on loans over the summer after just one season with the club, which led to the arrivals of Kolo Muani, Jeff Ekhator and Nick Woltemade during the most recent transfer window.

It took Kolo Muani until October to re-open his Serie A account for Juventus, nodding in the equaliser in a 1-1 draw away against Cagliari on Sunday. The Frenchman had scored eight goals from 16 appearances in the Italian top flight during a loan spell from Paris Saint-Germain in the second half of the 2024-25 season.

It has been suggested by outlets including Tuttosport that Spalletti is still facing more or less the exact same issues he faced when he first arrived at the club almost a year ago: The most obvious being that he doesn’t have enough options at centre-forward.

articles.title: Zverev celebrates becoming year-end No 1 with Bublik win in Shanghai
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev celebrated becoming the year-end No 1 with a 7-6 (8-6) 4-6 7-6 (7-1) victory over Alexander Bublik to reach the quarter-finals at the Shanghai Masters.
body: Zverev, who won the French Open and US Open this year, never looked 100 per cent comfortable, and admitted his "ankle was acting up" following his win.
The top seed will take on ninth seed Alex de Minaur next after the Australian produced one of his best performances of the year to beat Karen Khachanov in straight sets 6-3 6-4 to advance.

Zverev said: "I'm starting to feel my body more and more, but happy to be through because it was a difficult match. He's been playing amazing tennis this week. I think the most important thing was that I won today."

With current world No 1 Jannik Sinner out for the rest of 2026 due to a knee injury and Carlos Alcaraz unable to overtake Zverev this year, the German was competing for the first time since he clinched the year-end No 1 honours for the first time on Monday.

articles.title: Matt Shaw Trade Could Help Cubs’ Rotation, But Would Be Costly
articles.summary: A Matt Shaw trade is still a scenario, not a reported negotiation. But it is an easy one to picture this winter: move a blocked infielder, land a starter and patch the rotation.
body: Sports Illustrated’s Doug Schwamb floated the idea this week, suggesting Shaw could headline a deal for Los Angeles Angels left-hander Reid Detmers while admitting Shaw alone would not be enough. No report has the Cubs and Angels discussing it. That admission, though, is where the real debate starts.

Chicago gave up four young players across two deadline trades. Catcher Moisés Ballesteros and right-hander Mason McGwire went to Anaheim for reliever Ryan Zeferjahn, according to MLB.com. Ballesteros was Pipeline’s No. 1 Cubs prospect entering the year. McGwire, ranked 18th in the system, had made the Futures Game. A day earlier, Chicago landed Kevin Gausman from Toronto for Brett Bateman and Ty Southisene.

That is a lot of young talent for one deadline, and the rotation questions that were already circling have not gone away. The season ended in a Wild Card sweep, and the starters are still the biggest hole.

articles.title: A PL giant to fall? Newly-promoted clubs changing relegation equation
articles.summary: Hull, Coventry and Ipswich have already collected 24 points between them after six games, so the conversation is starting to shift from pre-season vibes on whether all three newly-promoted clubs will be relegated to which established Premier League names could be in the scrap for survival.
body: Hull City, Ipswich Town and Coventry City are all clear of the Premier League relegation zone after six games; does this put a supposedly safe mid-table club or a big-name team in genuine danger of relegation to the Championship this season?

The Premier League's newly-promoted sides have often struggled to bridge the gap, with two consecutive seasons in 2023/24 and 2024/25 seeing all three newcomers relegated before Leeds and Sunderland helped buck that trend last season.
The lesson teams are learning is that survival is possible when a promoted team gets their recruitment, organisation and mentality right.
Hull and Ipswich already have nine points, while Coventry, following their 4-1 hammering of Newcastle, are on six.
